title: A carrier helps a sugar cross
hook: Predict where the cargo ends up, then run the model.

knows: Cells have a plasma membrane separating inside from outside.
doesNotKnow: A glucose carrier can facilitate movement down a glucose concentration gradient without directly using ATP. Glc marks glucose and the purple shape represents a carrier; the selected particles are an illustration.

misconception: Everything crosses a cell membrane by the same mechanism.
objective: A glucose carrier can facilitate movement down a glucose concentration gradient without directly using ATP. Glc marks glucose and the purple shape represents a carrier; the selected particles are an illustration.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: In this model glucose is more concentrated outside than inside, and a suitable glucose carrier is present. Which direction is the initial net facilitated diffusion? A glucose carrier can facilitate movement down a glucose concentration gradient without directly using ATP. Glc marks glucose and the purple shape represents a carrier; the selected particles are an illustration.
Recall: What helps glucose cross a membrane in facilitated diffusion? Facilitated glucose diffusion uses a transport protein.
The diagram is schematic and represents only selected molecules, not trajectories or all particles.
